success_patterns: Six of the eight clues were solved by one move: find the single entity that recurs in the passage titles and snippets alongside the clue's distinctive details, then give it in the short form the titles use ('Love Story', 'Charles Evans Hughes', 'Thomas Hardy', 'Henry V', 'Billie Holiday'). The existing verbatim-match and recurring-entity rules already cover this.

Fractions and date ranges in the clue were translated into the form the passages use. '1/5 of the population' matched 'Yoruba make up 21 percent', and 'born between '46 & '64' matched the 'baby boomers' definition of 1946-1964. The agent picked the candidate whose figure or range fit, not the most-mentioned or largest group.

When the context was mostly off-topic (the Chipotle clue returned recipe and blog hits), the agent answered from its own knowledge of the well-known item the clue describes ('burrito', as the bare generic noun). It did not copy a brand item or a word from the noisy passages.
Answers were short and bare: no category word, no clue words repeated, plural kept for a 'these people' group ('baby boomers'), and the title's own wording kept ('Henry V', 'Love Story').

patch.reasoning: Most successes are covered by existing rules. Two behaviours are not stated and generalize. First, matching a clue's fraction, ratio or date range to the passages' percentages or definitions (for example 1/5 to 21%), choosing the closest fit. Second, trusting a self-sufficient descriptive clue and answering from knowledge when passages are irrelevant noise. Both fit under Rule 3's candidate-selection bullets and avoid heavy new structure.

edits.target: - If the context offers several candidates (a different player in the same article, a film and its song), pick the one that satisfies ALL distinctive details: exact numbers, team, years, place. Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - Translate approximate quantities and ranges in the clue into the form the passages use, then pick the closest fit, not the most-mentioned or largest candidate. 'About 1/5 the population of Nigeria' -> a passage saying 'Yoruba make up 21 percent' (not Hausa-Fulani, not Igbo 17%, not Ijaw 10%). "People born between '46 & '64" -> the passage defining that span ('baby boomers: born 1946-1964'). For a group described by 'these people', give the plural group label.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - If the passages are weak or off-topic (search hits on incidental words such as recipes, blogs or forums) but the clue itself describes a well-known thing ('a "giant flour tortilla" wrapped around meat, beans & cheese' -> 'burrito'), answer from your own knowledge. Use the generic common noun the description defines, not a brand item or a word from the noisy passages. Use any passage only to confirm. Never answer 'not answerable'.
